scope: A practical selection of free or free-tier OSINT resources for lawful research. Provider access and limits can change.

sections.name: Search and discovery
sections.description: Start broad, vary indexes and preserve the query that produced the lead.

tools.name: Google Advanced Search
tools.use_when: You need exact phrases, exclusions, date ranges, file types or site-restricted results.
tools.why: It turns an unstructured question into a reproducible query without memorising every operator.
tools.caution: Results are personalised, ranked and incomplete. Record the query, date and relevant result URL.

tools.name: Bing
tools.use_when: Google returns little, especially for recently indexed pages, images or Microsoft-hosted content.
tools.why: A different index often exposes pages and cached snippets missed by Google.
tools.caution: A snippet can be stale or assembled from text no longer present on the page.

tools.name: Brave Search
tools.use_when: You want an independent index and a second view of a keyword, name or domain.
tools.why: It reduces dependence on one search provider's ranking and coverage.
tools.caution: Privacy-focused search is not operational anonymity, and index coverage still has gaps.

sections.name: Web history and capture
sections.description: Recover historical pages, compare changes and preserve when a statement was visible.

tools.name: Wayback Machine
tools.use_when: A page changed, disappeared or previously exposed useful paths, branding or contact details.
tools.why: Timestamped captures can reconstruct historical content without relying on the live site.
tools.caution: Archived pages may request live third-party resources. Capture time is not necessarily publication time.

tools.name: Archive.today
tools.use_when: Wayback has no useful capture or you need a static snapshot of a public page.
tools.why: Its independent archive can preserve pages that another service missed.
tools.caution: Searching is passive; creating a capture causes the service to fetch the target.

tools.name: Common Crawl Index
tools.use_when: You need historical URLs or response records at larger scale.
tools.why: Open crawl indexes support reproducible bulk discovery and older-content recovery.
tools.caution: Crawls are sampled and historical. Preserve crawl ID, timestamp and digest.

sections.name: Domain, DNS and certificates
sections.description: Establish registration context, DNS state and certificate-linked names before clustering infrastructure.

tools.name: ICANN Lookup
tools.use_when: You need current registrar, status, nameserver and registration-date context.
tools.why: It queries authoritative registration-data services instead of an unknown WHOIS mirror.
tools.caution: Redaction and privacy services are normal. Registrant privacy is not suspicious and registrar choice is weak evidence.

tools.name: crt.sh
tools.use_when: You have a domain, certificate fingerprint or organisation string and want CT-linked names.
tools.why: Certificate Transparency can reveal historical and sibling hostnames without touching them.
tools.caution: A wildcard certificate shows issuance scope, not every hostname actually deployed. Certificate reuse is not actor attribution.

tools.name: DNSDumpster
tools.use_when: You want a quick visual inventory of public DNS records and related hosts for a domain.
tools.why: It provides a low-friction starting map before deeper record-by-record validation.
tools.caution: Validate every result with an authoritative or separately collected source; historical and current records can be mixed.

sections.name: IP and network intelligence
sections.description: Map an address to routing, hosting and observed service context without turning provider data into attribution.

tools.name: Shodan InternetDB
tools.use_when: You need a quick, unauthenticated view of ports, hostnames, tags and known CVEs associated with an IP.
tools.why: It is fast and script-friendly for first-pass enrichment.
tools.caution: The record is provider-collected and point-in-time. A CVE association is not proof of exploitability.

tools.name: BGP.tools
tools.use_when: You need prefix, ASN, upstream, downstream and route context around an IP.
tools.why: Routing context helps separate a workload, provider and surrounding address space.
tools.caution: ASN adjacency and shared hosting are leads, not evidence of common control.

tools.name: GreyNoise Community
tools.use_when: You want to know whether an IP was recently observed scanning the internet or belongs to a common benign service dataset.
tools.why: It helps distinguish routine internet noise from potentially targeted activity.
tools.caution: Its classification describes GreyNoise observations, not a universal reputation verdict. Free lookups are limited.

sections.name: Web artefacts and source code
sections.description: Pivot exact strings, response hashes, filenames and implementation details into related public material.

tools.name: urlscan.io
tools.use_when: You have a URL, domain, IP, ASN, certificate, filename or response hash from a web investigation.
tools.why: Existing scans expose redirects, requests, responses, screenshots and repeatable artefact pivots.
tools.caution: Search before submitting. Public scans disclose the full URL and can expose tokens, PII or investigation interest.

tools.name: GitHub Code Search
tools.use_when: You have an uncommon string, endpoint, typo, key, filename or code construction.
tools.why: Exact code matches can find public repositories, reused configuration and related samples.
tools.caution: Preserve the commit and blob. Forks, mirrors and copied code do not prove common authorship.

tools.name: grep.app
tools.use_when: You need fast exact-string or regular-expression search across indexed public GitHub code.
tools.why: Repository, path and language facets make broad code hunting easy without local cloning.
tools.caution: Open the original repository and verify the commit; indexing and freshness are incomplete.

sections.name: Usernames and social accounts
sections.description: Find candidate public profiles, then verify identity through content and cross-platform evidence.

tools.name: WhatsMyName
tools.use_when: You have a username and want quick candidate-account checks across many services.
tools.why: It is simple, transparent and useful for generating leads without installing a tool.
tools.caution: Username reuse is common. A matching handle is not proof that two accounts belong to the same person.

tools.name: Sherlock
tools.use_when: You need repeatable, local username checks that can be exported and documented.
tools.why: It automates public profile checks across many sites and keeps the workflow under analyst control.
tools.caution: False positives, rate limits and site changes are expected. Manually verify every meaningful result.

tools.name: Maigret
tools.use_when: You need username enumeration plus structured profile metadata from supported sites.
tools.why: Its reports can accelerate cross-platform triage and preserve a reproducible starting set.
tools.caution: Automated metadata can be stale or misparsed. Do not equate a username hit with identity resolution.

sections.name: Email and breach exposure
sections.description: Check exposure and reputation without collecting passwords or turning breach data into targeting material.

tools.name: Have I Been Pwned
tools.use_when: You need to check whether your own or an authorised address appears in known breach records.
tools.why: It provides breach names and exposure context without publishing passwords.
tools.caution: Use only for legitimate defensive checks. A breach appearance does not show that a current password is valid.

tools.name: EmailRep
tools.use_when: You need lightweight reputation and public-presence context around an email address.
tools.why: It combines several signals into a quick triage view and API response.
tools.caution: A reputation score is an assessment, not identity proof. Respect rate limits and privacy law.

tools.name: Hunter
tools.use_when: You are researching authorised organisational email patterns or publicly listed professional contacts.
tools.why: Domain search, source links and pattern confidence can validate corporate contact structure.
tools.caution: Do not use it for unsolicited targeting. Free quotas are limited and pattern-generated addresses require verification.

sections.name: Phone-number research
sections.description: Normalise a number, establish numbering context and look for public reporting without assuming caller identity.

tools.name: PhoneInfoga
tools.use_when: You need country, carrier-format and search-engine pivots from an international number.
tools.why: It structures basic number intelligence and repeatable public searches in one workflow.
tools.caution: Subscriber identity is usually unavailable. Caller ID can be spoofed, recycled or used by an SMS provider.

tools.name: libphonenumber demo
tools.use_when: You need to parse, validate and format an international phone number before searching it.
tools.why: Correct normalisation prevents missed results caused by spaces, trunk prefixes or country-code variants.
tools.caution: A technically valid number is not proof that it is assigned, active or controlled by the sender.

tools.name: Truecaller
tools.use_when: You want community label and spam-report context for a number.
tools.why: Crowdsourced names and spam categories can provide a useful lead when corroborated elsewhere.
tools.caution: Labels are user supplied and can be wrong. Never publish a person's identity from this source alone.

sections.name: Image and video verification
sections.description: Find earlier appearances, extract frames and test media claims without treating one forensic signal as a verdict.

tools.name: Google Lens
tools.use_when: You need visually similar images, text extraction, object recognition or possible source pages.
tools.why: Its broad image index and region selection work well for tracing reused visual elements.
tools.caution: Uploads leave your environment. Crop variants and verify dates rather than trusting result order.

tools.name: TinEye
tools.use_when: You want exact or transformed image matches and a sortable history of indexed copies.
tools.why: It is particularly useful for locating older versions and common edits.
tools.caution: Oldest indexed result is not necessarily the original publication, and no match does not prove novelty.

tools.name: InVID Verification Plugin
tools.use_when: You need video keyframes, reverse searches, metadata views and verification helpers.
tools.why: It reduces video verification into inspectable steps instead of one opaque score.
tools.caution: Metadata can be stripped or altered. Combine keyframes, source history, landmarks and timing evidence.

sections.name: Geolocation and maps
sections.description: Compare terrain, roads, street imagery, shadows and historical satellite context.

tools.name: Google Earth
tools.use_when: You need terrain, 3D context, satellite imagery or broad visual comparison around a location.
tools.why: It provides a fast spatial overview and measurement tools familiar to most investigators.
tools.caution: Imagery dates and resolution vary. Always record the imagery date shown in the interface.

tools.name: Mapillary
tools.use_when: Street View has no coverage or you need user-contributed street-level imagery from another date.
tools.why: Independent sequences can reveal signs, road layout and changes missed by one mapping provider.
tools.caution: Contributor timestamps and GPS positions may be imperfect; corroborate landmarks and direction.

tools.name: SunCalc
tools.use_when: A shadow direction or sun position can help test a claimed time or camera orientation.
tools.why: It turns date, time and coordinates into a simple sun-path model.
tools.caution: Weather, terrain, camera perspective and uncertain timestamps can overwhelm the apparent precision.

sections.name: Companies and public records
sections.description: Trace legal entities, officers, filings and sanctions as public-record leads, not guilt by association.

tools.name: OpenCorporates
tools.use_when: You need company names, jurisdictions, registration numbers, officers or filing links.
tools.why: Normalised company records make cross-jurisdiction entity discovery easier.
tools.caution: Names collide and records can lag. Confirm important facts in the named official registry.

tools.name: OCCRP Aleph
tools.use_when: You need cross-document search across public records, leaks and investigative datasets.
tools.why: Entity extraction and linked documents can expose relationships difficult to find through ordinary search.
tools.caution: A mention is not proof of wrongdoing. Read the source document and understand dataset provenance.

tools.name: OpenSanctions
tools.use_when: You need sanctions, politically exposed person and related-entity screening context.
tools.why: It aggregates many official lists into a searchable, structured dataset.
tools.caution: Potential matches require identity resolution. Similar names alone must never drive an accusation.

sections.name: Malware and threat intelligence
sections.description: Enrich hashes, URLs and infrastructure while keeping vendor labels and community submissions subordinate to evidence.

tools.name: VirusTotal
tools.use_when: You have a hash, URL, domain or IP and need detections, submissions and object relationships.
tools.why: Its cross-object view provides fast enrichment and historical leads from many sources.
tools.caution: Do not upload confidential files or private indicators. Zero detections does not mean benign.

tools.name: URLhaus
tools.use_when: You need malware-distribution URL, payload-hash and delivery context.
tools.why: It connects malicious download locations with collected payloads and time-bounded status.
tools.caution: It is for malware delivery, not phishing-only pages. A host may later be cleaned or reassigned.

tools.name: MalwareBazaar
tools.use_when: You have a malware hash, signature, tag or family lead and want sample metadata.
tools.why: It supports hash enrichment and clustering without requiring sample execution.
tools.caution: Downloads are live malware. Family names are community labels and can conflict across sources.

sections.name: Documents and datasets
sections.description: Find primary documents and structured datasets, then preserve their version and provenance.

tools.name: Google Dataset Search
tools.use_when: You need a public dataset by topic, publisher, geography or format.
tools.why: It indexes dataset metadata across many repositories from one search interface.
tools.caution: Assess publisher, licence, update date, methodology and completeness before analysis.

tools.name: DocumentCloud
tools.use_when: You need searchable primary documents published by journalists and research organisations.
tools.why: OCR, annotations and source collections make large documentary records easier to inspect.
tools.caution: OCR errors are common. Quote and cite the underlying page image, not only extracted text.

tools.name: data.europa.eu
tools.use_when: You need official European public-sector datasets and catalogue metadata.
tools.why: It provides a cross-country discovery layer with publisher and licence context.
tools.caution: Catalogue entries point to national providers with different quality, formats and update schedules.
